bull_bear.body:
- Owns a legacy land and property asset base (registered office at Coimbatore, Hindupur land holdings, Super Sara and B units in Andhra Pradesh) that is being systematically monetised
- Leasing of existing assets provides a stable stream of rental income and improved asset productivity
- Long operating history — the 64th Annual Report was presented for the financial year ended 31st March 2026
- Promoter and promoter-group backing: Chairman and Managing Director Mr. Sumanth Ramamurthi holds 17.16% and Elgi Electric and Industries Limited (Promoter Group) holds 1.39% of the share capital; the Director extended a loan to the Company that was settled against land
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Accounting-system audit trail deficiency flagged by the Statutory Auditors — The software/application used for maintaining Payroll and Property, Plant and Equipment & Intangible Assets does not have a feature of recording audit trail (edit log) both at application and database level, and the accounting software "Tally" lacks audit trail at the database level. This is a stated exception to an otherwise unqualified audit report and a direct internal-control weakness over the books of account; management has committed to implement the feature during the current financial year.
- Audit trail not enabled through the year — direct data changes unlogged — The Statutory Auditors record that the audit trail feature was not enabled at the database level throughout the year to log any direct data changes for "Tally". Unlogged direct database changes mean the integrity of the accounting records cannot be independently evidenced for the full period.
- Auditors unable to verify preservation of the audit trail for statutory record retention — Arising from the two audit-trail exceptions, the Statutory Auditors state they are unable to verify the preservation of the audit trail as per the statutory requirements for record retention. Management has undertaken to take appropriate corrective measures to ensure compliance with statutory record-retention norms and prevent recurrence.
- Listing-regulation compliance failures reported by the Secretarial Auditors — late integrated filing — Integrated filing (financial) for the quarter and year ended 31st March 2025, including audited results under Regulation 33(3) and related-party disclosure under Regulation 23(9), was submitted to BSE Limited on 24th May 2025 and to NSE on 26th May 2025, beyond the prescribed timeline of 23rd May 2025. Directors attribute the delay to administrative and other reasons and state subsequent filings were made in due course.
- Regulation 30 event disclosure lapses — unreported or belatedly reported events — The Secretarial Auditors report that the listed entity has not reported or has belatedly reported certain events on the stock exchange(s) under Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations. A recurring pattern of event-disclosure lapses is a market-integrity and enforcement risk; the entity undertakes there will be no such further instances going forward.
- Non-submission of the declaration of unmodified opinion with annual audited results — The listed entity did not submit the Declaration regarding unmodified opinion in the Audit Report required under the proviso to Regulation 33(3)(d) while publishing annual audited results for the quarter and year ended 31st March 2025 on both stock exchanges. Described as inadvertent, with an undertaking to comply in future. This is the third distinct Secretarial-Audit compliance exception in one year.
- Concentrated related-party dealing requiring shareholder approval — Pursuant to Regulation 23 of the Listing Regulations the Company obtained shareholder approval to enter into MATERIAL related party transactions with two of its related parties, with particulars given in Form AOC-2 annexed as Annexure 1. Directors state all related-party transactions are at arm's length and in the ordinary course of business, but material transactions with promoter-connected counterparties remain a structural governance exposure.
- Risk management is policy-level only, with no risk register or committee detail disclosed — The Company states it has developed and implemented a Risk Management Policy under Section 134(3)(n) envisaging identification of risk and procedures for assessment and minimisation. No specific business, market, tenant, counterparty or regulatory risks are enumerated anywhere in the routed text, and no Risk Management Committee composition or ERM framework is described.

business.body: The Company has exited its textiles business and is currently focusing on the rental business. It has leased out certain properties of the SUPER SARA unit under operating lease arrangements, which are generating a significant revenue, and is optimising utilisation of its existing assets by leasing to produce a stable stream of rental income and improved asset productivity. It is additionally pursuing systematic monetisation of its land assets at the registered office and at Hindupur through development partners.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Exit from textiles: the Company has exited its textiles business, discontinued operations in the "Textiles" segment, and now operates in the "Rental and Real Estate Services" business segment.
- Optimise utilisation of existing assets by leasing, to produce a stable stream of rental income and improved asset productivity; certain properties of the SUPER SARA unit are leased out under operating lease arrangements.
- Systematic monetisation of the Company's land assets — through a development partner at the registered office project and through a proposed Joint Development Agreement for the Hindupur land — described as contributing to future revenue streams.
- Reduce outstanding liabilities and strengthen the financial position by optimising the asset base, including the transfer of a small parcel of registered-office land against a Director's loan.
- Leverage the expertise and resources of an external development partner (not a related party for the Hindupur arrangement) rather than developing land in-house.
- The routed governance text states no dividend, payout, buyback, debt-reduction or reinvestment POLICY. What it does show is the mechanism actually used in FY2025-26: two one-time related-party sale agreements for property owned by the Company, both Board-approved on 29th August 2025 for the period September 2025 to March 2026, stated to be carried out on an arm's length basis with NIL advances paid — one with Mr. Sumanth Ramamurthi up to a maximum aggregate value of Rs 7 Crores and one with Elgi Electric and Industries Limited up to a maximum aggregate value of 2 crores. No dividend philosophy, gearing target or reinvestment intent is articulated in this bundle.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Super Spinning Mills has no manufacturing capex or capacity-addition programme in FY2025-26; having exited textiles, its expansion activity is entirely real-estate development of its own land bank, executed through external development partners rather than by the Company. Two projects are named. First, a project proposed at the registered office (Coimbatore), for which shareholder consent was obtained on 23rd July 2025, is being undertaken through a development partner who is currently in the process of obtaining the requisite approvals, sanctions and permissions from the concerned governmental and regulatory authorities; upon receipt of approvals and commencement of development activities it is expected to facilitate systematic monetisation of the Company's land assets and contribute to future revenue streams. No commissioning date, project cost or built-up area is stated. Second, the Company sought shareholder consent on 7th March 2026 through postal ballot to develop a parcel of land in Hindupur by entering into a Joint Development Agreement for the development of a portion of its land holdings into commercial / residential plots; it is in the process of identifying potential buyer(s) and a joint development partner (not being a related party) and negotiating consideration and other terms, with the development expected to monetise land assets while leveraging the partner's expertise and resources. Alongside these, the Company transferred a small parcel of land at the registered office to its Chairman and Managing Director and to Elgi Electric and Industries Limited (shareholder consent 2nd October 2025) to reduce outstanding liabilities, and continues to lease out certain properties of the SUPER SARA unit under operating lease arrangements as part of optimising utilisation of existing assets. No rupee quantum, timeline or phasing is disclosed for either development project in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Leased properties of the SUPER SARA unit under operating lease arrangements are stated to be generating a significant revenue.
- Leasing of existing assets is stated to result in a stable stream of rental income and improved asset productivity.
- The registered-office development project is expected to facilitate systematic monetisation of land assets and contribute to future revenue streams, once approvals are received and development commences.
- The proposed Hindupur Joint Development Agreement is expected to facilitate systematic monetisation of land assets while leveraging the development partner's expertise and resources.

First, a project proposed at the registered office (Coimbatore), for which shareholder consent was obtained on 23rd July 2025, is being undertaken through a development partner who is currently in the process of obtaining the requisite approvals, sanctions and permissions from the concerned governmental and regulatory authorities; upon receipt of approvals and commencement of development activities it is expected to facilitate systematic monetisation of the Company's land assets and contribute to future revenue streams. No commissioning date, project cost or built-up area is stated. Second, the Company sought shareholder consent on 7th March 2026 through postal ballot to develop a parcel of land in Hindupur by entering into a Joint Development Agreement for the development of a portion of its land holdings into commercial / residential plots; it is in the process of identifying potential buyer(s) and a joint development partner (not being a related party) and negotiating consideration and other terms, with the development expected to monetise land assets while leveraging the partner's expertise and resources. Alongside these, the Company transferred a small parcel of land at the registered office to its Chairman and Managing Director and to Elgi Electric and Industries Limited (shareholder consent 2nd October 2025) to reduce outstanding liabilities, and continues to lease out certain properties of the SUPER SARA unit under operating lease arrangements as part of optimising utilisation of existing assets. No rupee quantum, timeline or phasing is disclosed for either development project in the routed text.

risks.risk: Accounting-system audit trail deficiency flagged by the Statutory Auditors
risks.note: The software/application used for maintaining Payroll and Property, Plant and Equipment & Intangible Assets does not have a feature of recording audit trail (edit log) both at application and database level, and the accounting software "Tally" lacks audit trail at the database level. This is a stated exception to an otherwise unqualified audit report and a direct internal-control weakness over the books of account; management has committed to implement the feature during the current financial year.

risks.risk: Audit trail not enabled through the year — direct data changes unlogged
risks.note: The Statutory Auditors record that the audit trail feature was not enabled at the database level throughout the year to log any direct data changes for "Tally". Unlogged direct database changes mean the integrity of the accounting records cannot be independently evidenced for the full period.

risks.risk: Auditors unable to verify preservation of the audit trail for statutory record retention
risks.note: Arising from the two audit-trail exceptions, the Statutory Auditors state they are unable to verify the preservation of the audit trail as per the statutory requirements for record retention. Management has undertaken to take appropriate corrective measures to ensure compliance with statutory record-retention norms and prevent recurrence.

risks.risk: Listing-regulation compliance failures reported by the Secretarial Auditors — late integrated filing
risks.note: Integrated filing (financial) for the quarter and year ended 31st March 2025, including audited results under Regulation 33(3) and related-party disclosure under Regulation 23(9), was submitted to BSE Limited on 24th May 2025 and to NSE on 26th May 2025, beyond the prescribed timeline of 23rd May 2025. Directors attribute the delay to administrative and other reasons and state subsequent filings were made in due course.

risks.risk: Regulation 30 event disclosure lapses — unreported or belatedly reported events
risks.note: The Secretarial Auditors report that the listed entity has not reported or has belatedly reported certain events on the stock exchange(s) under Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations. A recurring pattern of event-disclosure lapses is a market-integrity and enforcement risk; the entity undertakes there will be no such further instances going forward.

risks.risk: Non-submission of the declaration of unmodified opinion with annual audited results
risks.note: The listed entity did not submit the Declaration regarding unmodified opinion in the Audit Report required under the proviso to Regulation 33(3)(d) while publishing annual audited results for the quarter and year ended 31st March 2025 on both stock exchanges. Described as inadvertent, with an undertaking to comply in future. This is the third distinct Secretarial-Audit compliance exception in one year.

risks.risk: Concentrated related-party dealing requiring shareholder approval
risks.note: Pursuant to Regulation 23 of the Listing Regulations the Company obtained shareholder approval to enter into MATERIAL related party transactions with two of its related parties, with particulars given in Form AOC-2 annexed as Annexure 1. Directors state all related-party transactions are at arm's length and in the ordinary course of business, but material transactions with promoter-connected counterparties remain a structural governance exposure.

risks.risk: Risk management is policy-level only, with no risk register or committee detail disclosed
risks.note: The Company states it has developed and implemented a Risk Management Policy under Section 134(3)(n) envisaging identification of risk and procedures for assessment and minimisation. No specific business, market, tenant, counterparty or regulatory risks are enumerated anywhere in the routed text, and no Risk Management Committee composition or ERM framework is described.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Super Spinning Mills Limited is a 64-year-old Coimbatore-based company that has exited its textiles business and now operates solely in the Rental and Real Estate Services segment, monetising its legacy land and plant assets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company has exited its textiles business and is currently focusing on the rental business. It has leased out certain properties of the SUPER SARA unit under operating lease arrangements, which are generating a significant revenue, and is optimising utilisation of its existing assets by leasing to produce a stable stream of rental income and improved asset productivity. It is additionally pursuing systematic monetisation of its land assets at the registered office and at Hindupur through development partners.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Elgi Electric and Industries Limited — related party: Part of the Promoter Group; holds 1.39% of the share capital of the Company. Mr. Sumanth Ramamurthi (Chairman and Managing Director), Mr. Sanjay Krishna Ramamurthi and Mr. Nikhil Govind Ramamurthi, Directors of the Company, hold Directorship in Elgi Electric and Industries Limited and hold more than 2% of its paid-up share capital. Counterparty to a one-time sale agreement for property owned by the Company, Board-approved 29th August 2025, duration September 2025 to March 2026, stated to be on an arm's length basis with NIL advances paid.
- Mr. Sumanth Ramamurthi — related party: Chairman and Managing Director and Promoter, holding 17.16% of the shares. Counterparty to a one-time sale agreement for property owned by the Company, Board-approved 29th August 2025, duration September 2025 to March 2026, stated to be on an arm's length basis with NIL advances paid. Mr. Sanjay Krishna Ramamurthi and Mr. Nikhil Govind Ramamurthi, Directors, are his relatives and are interested through their relative.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Rental and Real Estate Services:** Operating lease of properties of the SUPER SARA unit, Land development / monetisation through development partners
- **Textiles:** Discontinued during the financial year ended 31st March 2026

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic property rental / leasing (India)
- Commercial / residential plotted development at Hindupur, Andhra Pradesh (proposed)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Leased properties of the SUPER SARA unit under operating lease arrangements are stated to be generating a significant revenue.
- Leasing of existing assets is stated to result in a stable stream of rental income and improved asset productivity.
- The registered-office development project is expected to facilitate systematic monetisation of land assets and contribute to future revenue streams, once approvals are received and development commences.
- The proposed Hindupur Joint Development Agreement is expected to facilitate systematic monetisation of land assets while leveraging the development partner's expertise and resources.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Exit from textiles: the Company has exited its textiles business, discontinued operations in the "Textiles" segment, and now operates in the "Rental and Real Estate Services" business segment.
- Optimise utilisation of existing assets by leasing, to produce a stable stream of rental income and improved asset productivity; certain properties of the SUPER SARA unit are leased out under operating lease arrangements.
- Systematic monetisation of the Company's land assets — through a development partner at the registered office project and through a proposed Joint Development Agreement for the Hindupur land — described as contributing to future revenue streams.
- Reduce outstanding liabilities and strengthen the financial position by optimising the asset base, including the transfer of a small parcel of registered-office land against a Director's loan.
- Leverage the expertise and resources of an external development partner (not a related party for the Hindupur arrangement) rather than developing land in-house.
- The routed governance text states no dividend, payout, buyback, debt-reduction or reinvestment POLICY. What it does show is the mechanism actually used in FY2025-26: two one-time related-party sale agreements for property owned by the Company, both Board-approved on 29th August 2025 for the period September 2025 to March 2026, stated to be carried out on an arm's length basis with NIL advances paid — one with Mr. Sumanth Ramamurthi up to a maximum aggregate value of Rs 7 Crores and one with Elgi Electric and Industries Limited up to a maximum aggregate value of 2 crores. No dividend philosophy, gearing target or reinvestment intent is articulated in this bundle.
